theme_scores.justification: The single line 'It will be reviewed.' gives no detail on success measures, testing, evaluation timetable, or consultation plans.

reasoning: The extract for this section consists of a single, unsupported sentence: 'It will be reviewed.' This falls well short of what the framework requires. There is no indication of what success measures will be used to judge the policy's effectiveness, no mention of any plans to test the ban before or during rollout, no explanation of what data or outcomes will be measured to assess impact, no timetable for when a review will happen, and no statement about how or whether the results of any review will be published or acted upon. There is also no reference to consultation being used to inform testing or evaluation plans. The phrase 'reviewed' is vague enough that it could mean anything from an informal internal check to a full public evaluation, and without further detail a reader cannot judge whether this constitutes meaningful evaluation at all. The strongest possible counter-reading is that the mere presence of a commitment to review at all shows some minimal forward planning, which is why this does not fall to the very bottom of nothing at all being said. But it does not rise even to level 1, since level 1 requires at least 'some indication of success measures', and none are given here. To reach a higher level, the document would need to specify what will be measured, when the review will take place, how results will be used, and why testing was or wasn't undertaken.
